title: Urge Battle Dice
core_goal: I do not have to obey an urge. I can experience it without acting on it.

urge_surfing_reminder.title: Remember: Urges Are Waves
urge_surfing_reminder.message: An urge rises, peaks, and falls. I don't need to fight it or feed it. I can observe it, breathe through it, and let it pass.
steps: Notice: I am having an urge.
Name it: This is an urge, not an instruction.
Wait and let the wave change.
Choose my action instead of obeying the impulse.

motivation_quotes: An urge is a feeling, not a command.
I don't need to win forever. I only need to win this moment.
The urge will pass whether I feed it or not.
I can feel uncomfortable without escaping into stimulation.
My future self is built by what I do in moments like this.
I am training my brain every time I choose restraint.
I don't have to negotiate with an impulse.
Pause first. Decide later.
This feeling is temporary. My goal is bigger.
I am the person making the decision, not the urge.
Discomfort is not danger.
I can surf this wave without drowning in it.
Every resisted urge is practice.
I don't need perfection. I need the next good decision.
My attention belongs to me.
I choose what I consume.
The easiest choice isn't always the choice I want.
Ten minutes of discomfort can protect hours of regret.
I can redirect my attention.
I don't have to act just because my brain asks.
Let the urge be there. Let it leave.
I can tolerate this moment.
My impulse is loud, but I don't have to listen.
I am learning to sit with boredom.
I am building self-control one decision at a time.

activities.activity: Take 20 slow breaths. Count each exhale.
Stand up and slowly stretch your entire body.
Walk around your home without your phone.
Do 20 squats, rest, then repeat once.
Drink a full glass of water slowly.
Look around and name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear.
Go outside and walk for a few minutes.
Do 10 push-ups or an easier variation.
activities.focus: Turn the urge into physical action.

activities.activity: Take a cool or refreshing face wash.
Put your phone in another room and sit somewhere else.
Write: 'What am I feeling right now?' and answer honestly.
activities.focus: Identify the emotion behind the urge.

activities.activity: Write three reasons you want to break this habit.
Write one thing your future self will thank you for.
Do a 3-minute room cleanup.
Fold or organize some clothes.
activities.focus: Give your hands something useful to do.

activities.activity: Wash a few dishes.
Organize your desk.
Read two pages of a physical book.
Write 5 sentences about what you want your life to look like in one year.
Write down exactly what triggered the urge.
Sit quietly and watch the urge like a wave for 3 minutes.
Rate the urge from 1-10. Re-rate it after 3 minutes.
activities.focus: See that urges change over time.

activities.activity: Close your eyes and notice where the urge appears in your body.
Take slow breaths while repeating: 'I can let this pass.'
Walk while counting your steps from 1 to 100.
Look outside and describe everything you can see in detail.
Do 30 jumping jacks, then breathe slowly.
Hold a plank for as long as comfortable, rest, and repeat.
Stretch your neck, shoulders, back, hips, and legs.
Walk up and down a safe set of stairs slowly.
Write a short letter to your future self.
Write: 'If I obey this urge, how will I feel afterward?'
Write: 'If I resist this urge, how will I feel afterward?'
Write down one thing you are proud of accomplishing recently.
Write three things you are grateful for.
Plan the next hour of your day.
Choose one tiny task you've been avoiding and start it.
Put away 10 objects that are out of place.
activities.focus: Use the urge as a cue for productivity.

activities.activity: Make your bed carefully.
Prepare a healthy snack or drink.
activities.focus: Care for yourself instead of escaping.

activities.activity: Write one sentence describing the person you want to become.
Repeat slowly: 'I choose my actions even when my feelings are strong.'
Imagine the urge as a wave and watch it rise and fall.
Set a 5-minute timer and simply sit without entertainment.
Do slow breathing: inhale 4 seconds, exhale 6 seconds.
Write down the exact thought trying to convince you to give in.
Answer the thought with: 'Maybe, but I choose not to.'
Take a 5-minute phone-free walk and notice your surroundings.
Write today's most important goal and take one step toward it.
Sit quietly, breathe, and repeat: 'I don't need to win forever. I only need to win this moment.'
